summary: ICIS (Sep 18) marked Vietnam PP yarn/inj higher; crude reversal stalled talks
Domestic supply tight on maintenance/shutdowns; buyers prefer local material
North PP homo VND 40,000-42,000/kg; BSR facing ~2-week delivery delays
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, September 18, the general PP yarn/injection price level in Vietnam rose USD 30/tonne at the low end and USD 70/tonne at the high end last week, to USD 1,240-1,330/tonne/CFR. Across the wider region, PP price levels rose in all markets; in Southeast Asia specifically, PP block copolymer rose USD 50/tonne (to USD 1,400-1,450/tonne/CFR) and PP random copolymer rose USD 80/tonne from the week before to USD 1,500/tonne/CFR…

Prices rose on the boost from climbing crude oil prices, so when oil reversed lower from midweek, negotiation activity also stalled. In China, both PP producers and downstream manufacturers are under heavy margin pressure from high input costs.

Domestic supply has tightened due to planned maintenance and plant shutdowns, so Chinese suppliers showed little interest in negotiating lower prices. There are reports that some downstream producers may further cut operating rates if PP prices remain high.

In Southeast Asia, buyers running low on resin inventories were forced to accept higher prices, but still preferred domestic material that can be delivered to the warehouse with shorter lead times. Imported supply is scarce, with October-delivery volumes very limited. Some sellers believe the PP price uptrend will gradually lose momentum as buyer resistance grows, unless crude oil and upstream chemical prices spike again. With a major Southeast Asian producer restarting its PP production line and Chinese export volumes expected to rise as the country's domestic demand slows in October, many expect supply to be more abundant next month.

Back in the Vietnamese market, on the first trading day of the new week today, September 21, deal closings in PP were fairly limited, as most sellers had not yet accepted price cuts while buyers were fairly cautious about far-forward offers.

A southern source said offer levels for PP yarn/injection of domestic plants such as Hyosung Vina and BSR, as well as some standard imported PP grades of Korean and Chinese origin, ranged from VND 40,500-41,000/kg including VAT. Prices held flat from late last week, or eased slightly for far-forward offers, while spot PP remained fairly scarce.

“Some southern customers who contracted BSR's PP have been facing delivery delays of about two weeks now; some new buyers inquiring were told by the supplier that October-delivery material was sold out and that sales of early-November 2026-delivery material had begun,” a southern source said.

Similarly, in the north, offer levels for PP homopolymer of various origins ranged from VND 40,000-42,000/kg including VAT; transaction prices for domestically sourced PP yarn/injection were commonly at VND 40,500-41,000/kg including VAT, flat to slightly lower than late last week. PP copolymer, Film and coating grades also saw little price adjustment today.

summary: ICIS (Sep 18) PE up across board, but overly steep rise not accepted
LLDPE Film deals VND 41,000-43,000/kg; HDPE/LDPE pausing after weeks up
paras: According to ICIS assessments released on last week's final trading day, September 18, PE price levels in Vietnam rose across the board last week. Specifically: LDPE rose USD 160/tonne to USD 1,490-1,580/tonne/CFR; LLDPE Film rose USD 75-80/tonne to USD 1,230-1,330/tonne/CFR; HDPE Film rose USD 30/tonne at the low end but held flat at the high end, ranging USD 1,240-1,320/tonne/CFR; and HDPE injection and blow both rose USD 30/tonne, at USD 1,170-1,220/tonne/CFR and USD 1,200-1,230/tonne/CFR respectively.

PE prices rose mainly due to a combination of high production costs at some regional suppliers and increased demand from downstream manufacturers (converters) — firms holding low inventories in some markets. In Southeast Asia, suppliers simultaneously announced sharp price increases and achieved some success; some buyers running out of stock accepted notably higher prices to secure prompt or very-short-lead-time cargoes.

However, firms holding enough inventory to sustain operations until mid-October — when competitively priced imports from the US are expected to arrive in Asia — strongly resisted the new price levels. Middle Eastern supply remained short due to persistent uncertainty over shipping times and routes, amid escalating US-Iran conflict in the Middle East.

In Vietnam, PE import offers all trended higher last week, while negotiation and trading volumes fell sharply. In particular, from midweek, when oil prices reversed lower, resistance to the high price levels intensified. By the weekend, some suppliers had to lower their offers after raising them too steeply early in the week. PTT of Thailand, for example, offered LDPE, LLDPE and HDPE up sharply by USD 130-150/tonne early in the week but by the weekend cut its LDPE Film offer by USD 100/tonne (to USD 1,550/tonne/CIF) and its LLDPE and HDPE offers by USD 20-50/tonne to USD 1,450/tonne/CIF…

Today, September 21, one familiar distributor adjusted its offers for some Chinese-plant PE products to the Vietnamese market, with LLDPE Film offers mostly down USD 20-30/tonne from the previous week; LLDPE injection, roto, mLLDPE and LDPE grades held flat.

Specifically, import offers for oil-based LLDPE Film of ZPC, Wanhua, Yulong and Huatai origin were commonly in the USD 1,290-1,300/tonne/FOB range. Offers for LLDPE injection and roto grades were commonly at USD 1,330-1,340/tonne/FOB… Due to elevated freight rates, the CIF price to Vietnam adds about USD 30-40/tonne over the FOB offers above. Conversely, offers for STL (China) HDPE Film FS7000 today rose a further USD 10/tonne from the previous week to USD 1,380-1,390/tonne/CIF…

Domestically, last week many traders offered some Middle Eastern-origin LLDPE Film grades at VND 44,000-45,000/kg including VAT for prompt delivery, given scarce trading inventories. Chinese-origin LLDPE Film was offered up to VND 41,000-42,000/kg including VAT…

Today, according to sources, transaction prices for LLDPE Film across origins were commonly ranging VND 41,000-43,000/kg including VAT depending on origin, lower at the high end (as offers pushed up to VND 44,000-45,000/kg closed no deals).

“Some manufacturers of finished goods made from LLDPE feedstock said the finished products they make are contracted to customers at below VND 40,000/kg including VAT, so resin prices rising above VND 40,000/kg including VAT while they cannot yet raise finished-goods prices for end customers means producing at a loss,” a source analyzed.

LDPE and HDPE grades saw little price adjustment today, with the continuous rise of recent weeks now pausing. Offer levels for HDPE Film/yarn/injection were commonly in the VND 41,000-45,000/kg including VAT range; LDPE offers commonly in the VND 43,000-46,000/kg including VAT range…

summary: Dalian PVC futures fell 54 USD last week but Vietnam offers hold firm
AGC offered Asahimas Indonesia K66; oil-based imports 820-850 CIF
Domestic coal-based SG-5 steady at VND 23,000-23,500/kg; buyers waiting
paras: Last week, after five trading days, China's PVC futures (futures contracts on the Dalian Commodity Exchange) fell sharply by USD 54/tonne, dragging spot PVC prices down USD 37/tonne, even as import PVC prices held flat. On the first trading day of the new week today, September 21, PVC futures edged up nearly USD 3/tonne, halting a five-day losing streak and reflecting the cost pressure suppliers are facing.

In Vietnam today, September 21, AGC Group offered October 2026-delivery PVC from the Asahimas Indonesia (ASC) plant to Vietnam. ASC's K66 PVC was offered at USD 850-860/tonne/CIF this month, up sharply by USD 90-100/tonne from the previous month's offer. The distributor noted that volumes were limited, mainly due to freight issues. Offers for PVC from the Vinythai Thailand (AVT) plant had not yet been announced.

This development further shored up import offer levels for (oil-based) PVC to the Vietnamese market in the USD 820-850/tonne/CIF range. Last week, South Korea's LG Chem offered October-cargo PVC imports (LG Chem's familiar grades include LS100, LS100H…) to Vietnam at USD 810/tonne/CIF, excluding the 5% import duty. Japan's Taiyo settled TH1000 PVC for October delivery to Vietnam at USD 850-860/tonne/CIF. SCG of Thailand offered October 2026-delivery PVC at USD 841-850/tonne/CIF…

Domestically, PVC offer prices from distributors and trading firms saw little adjustment today. In the south, large customers are waiting for October-cargo PVC offers from the two domestic plants — AGC Vina and TPC Vina — to further assess the trend. In the north, most market participants judged that oil-based PVC prices in late September may hold steady in the VND 24,000-25,000/kg including VAT range.

Similarly, for coal-based PVC, offer prices from major distributors and trading firms were commonly holding in the VND 23,000-23,500/kg including VAT range in the north… No sellers have yet cut prices, even though coal-based PVC prices in China fell considerably last week.
